output.name: Kessal

anatomy.part: head and watching eye of the heron
tip of the back crest plume
breast, where the neck meets the body
left knee, bent in the shallows
right foot standing in the pool
the kelp pool at the water's edge

output.myth: Before the cut, Kessal was a fisher's wife who would not leave the kelp pool when the ebb ran out. Her man called to her from the boat. She lifted one foot, then the other, and found she could not set either down again. Mother Hesk, who keeps count of everything that stands still, wound her into the Lamp Road as a mark. Aun laughed from the sky and said a post is no use to a net. Tavo came down the cliff and shook the water off her wings, and still she did not move. Kael has cast for her many times and never caught her, because she has not fallen. She is only waiting for the water to turn. Whoever stands that long at a pool is said to get the best fish. Old women say this is true. Old women have also stood that long, and the fish were not the point.
output.verse:
Still post in the pool,
the tide will turn and the fish
come to the patient.
